name: EBITDA_L2_growth_roic_harmonic
mechanism: Within a broad industry, an EV/EBITDA multiple capitalizes cash flow, so it should differ mainly by expected growth and by the return earned on reinvestment (higher ROIC means growth creates more value), with size proxying for risk. Picking the nearest peers on these value drivers inside a 2-digit SIC group keeps business risk comparable while matching the drivers of the multiple, and the harmonic mean limits the pull of peers with very high multiples.
prediction: Median |ln error| below the L3/L2 industry median baseline (0.333) in at least 3 of 4 exploration years, with a pooled median of 0.32 or lower.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=10, harmonic_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback []
critic_reason: Matching on growth and ROIC, the two fundamental drivers of an EBITDA multiple, with size as a risk proxy inside a 2-digit industry is a clear mechanism, the recipe implements it directly, and the prediction can be checked year by year.

name: EBITDA_L3_leverage_capex_median
mechanism: Firms in the same 3-digit industry that also look alike on leverage, reinvestment needs and growth should share an EV/EBITDA multiple. Capex intensity separates EBITDA that turns into free cash flow from EBITDA that must be reinvested, and net debt/EBITDA captures financial risk and the cost of capital. A small peer set with a median aggregate stays robust to outliers.
prediction: Pooled median |ln error| at or below 0.33, and lower than the Bhojraj-Lee warranted-multiple peers baseline (0.380) in all 4 exploration years.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank capex_intensity 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5, sales_growth_1y 1, log_assets 0.5 | k=6, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []
critic_reason: Capex intensity (how much EBITDA turns into free cash flow) and net debt/EBITDA (financial risk) are sensible extra drivers of EV/EBITDA within a narrow industry, the rank features match the stated mechanism, the fallback chain is sensible, and the prediction is falsifiable.

name: EBITDA_crossindustry_fundamentals
mechanism: If the multiple is set by fundamentals (growth, profitability, reinvestment, size) rather than by industry labels, then the nearest peers on those fundamentals across the whole cross-section should value a firm about as well as industry peers, and better for firms with few or mismatched industry peers. A large k with a harmonic mean averages away idiosyncratic noise.
prediction: Pooled median |ln error| within 0.02 of the industry median baseline (no worse than 0.353), and better than the warranted-multiple regression (0.357) in at least 3 of 4 years.
compact: EV/EBITDA | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, ebitda_margin 0.5, capex_intensity 0.5, log_assets 0.5 | k=20, harmonic_mean, min_peers=3
critic_reason: This is a distinct economic test (fundamentals versus industry labels, in the spirit of warranted-multiple peers), the screen-free ranking on growth, profitability, reinvestment and size implements it faithfully, and the prediction gives explicit thresholds against two baselines.

name: Sales_L2_margin_growth_harmonic
mechanism: EV/Sales is roughly EV/EBITDA times EBITDA margin, so firms with different margins cannot share a sales multiple; matching on EBITDA margin (most weight), gross margin and growth inside a 2-digit industry gets rid of the main source of EV/Sales dispersion. The harmonic mean reduces the effect of a few richly valued peers.
prediction: Pooled median |ln error| below 0.52, beating the industry median baseline (0.603) in all 4 exploration years.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2 | rank ebitda_margin 2, gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=8, harmonic_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback []
critic_reason: The identity EV/Sales = EV/EBITDA x EBITDA margin makes margin matching a well-grounded mechanism, the heavy weight on ebitda_margin within a 2-digit industry implements it, and the prediction is falsifiable.

name: Sales_marginband_crossindustry
mechanism: A sales multiple is mostly a capitalized margin, so a hard band on EBITDA margin across all industries makes peers economically comparable even when SIC codes differ. Ranking the in-band firms on gross margin, growth and size then refines for pricing power, expected growth and risk; the median protects against outliers.
prediction: Pooled median |ln error| below 0.55, beating the industry median baseline (0.603) in at least 3 of 4 exploration years.

name: EBITDA_crossindustry_fundamentals
mechanism: If multiples reflect fundamentals rather than industry labels, firms anywhere in the market with similar growth, returns on capital, R&D and capital intensity, and leverage should trade at similar EV/EBITDA. A larger peer set (k=20) and harmonic mean reduce noise from the loss of the industry anchor.
prediction: Pooled median |ln error| within 0.03 of the industry median (below 0.36) and beats the Bhojraj-Lee warranted-multiple peers (0.380) in at least 3 of 4 years.
compact: EV/EBITDA | rank sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, rnd_intensity 1, capex_intensity 0.5, debt_to_assets 0.5 | k=20, harmonic_mean, min_peers=3
critic_reason: R&D intensity has not been tried and gives a specific reason for EV/EBITDA dispersion (expensed R&D lowers EBITDA, so R&D-heavy firms trade at higher EBITDA multiples); the recipe implements the cross-industry fundamentals idea and the prediction is falsifiable. Note that dropping candidates with missing R&D will shrink peer pools for low-R&D targets.

name: Sales_L2_margin_matched_harmonic
mechanism: EV/Sales equals EV/EBITDA times EBITDA margin, so margin is the dominant driver of the sales multiple; matching on EBITDA and gross margin within a 2-digit industry, plus growth, should remove most of the dispersion that ruins a plain industry EV/Sales median. The harmonic mean guards against high-multiple outliers.
prediction: Pooled median |ln error| below 0.55 and beats the industry median (0.603) in all 4 exploration years.

critic_reason: This is g01-04 with k changed from 8 to 10, and it differs from g02-04 and g03-04 only in one weight and the aggregator, which is exactly the trivial-variant case.

name: Sales_margin_band_crossindustry
mechanism: Because EV/Sales scales with profitability, a hard band on EBITDA margin across all industries groups firms that convert sales to cash at the same rate; ranking further on margin, growth, R&D intensity (future margins not yet in EBITDA) and size picks peers with similar value per dollar of sales.
prediction: Beats the industry median EV/Sales (0.603) on pooled median |ln error| and in at least 3 of 4 years.
compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank ebitda_margin 2, sales_growth_1y 1, rnd_intensity 0.5, log_sales 0.5 | k=15, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.1] -> []
critic_reason: Compared with the margin-band recipes g01-05 and g02-05, this adds a new, economically motivated feature (R&D intensity as future margin that EBITDA does not yet show) and a size control; the screens and ranks match the mechanism and the prediction is falsifiable.

name: Sales_L3_margin_turnover_tight
mechanism: Within a 3-digit industry, firms with the same gross and EBITDA margins and asset turnover have the same economic model (pricing power and capital required per dollar of sales), so their sales multiples should converge. A small peer set (k=6) keeps only the closest business-model twins.
prediction: Pooled median |ln error| below 0.58 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebitda_margin 2, gross_margin 1, asset_turnover 0.5 | k=6, harmonic_mean, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []
critic_reason: This is close to g01-06 and g02-06 (L3 screen ranked on EBITDA margin and asset turnover, k=6-8, L2 fallback), with only growth swapped for gross margin, and dropping growth, a main driver of EV/Sales, weakens the case that these 'business-model twins' should trade at the same sales multiple.
